items.followUp: Write four advantages of an electron microscope over a light microscope.

rubric.why: Electron microscopes magnify much more than light microscopes.
rubric.description: States that an electron microscope has very high magnification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its much greater magnifying power.

rubric.why: Its high resolving power lets it distinguish very small details.
rubric.description: Mentions its high resolution or resolving power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it can distinguish details that a light microscope cannot.

rubric.why: Its high magnification and resolution make very small objects such as viruses visible.
rubric.description: Gives viruses as an example of something it can be used to observe.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example such as viruses.

rubric.why: It can reveal fine details inside cells.
rubric.description: Mentions observing cell organelles or fine cellular structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the study of organelles or cell ultrastructure.

modelAnswer: An electron microscope provides much higher magnification than a light microscope.
Its greater resolving power reveals finer details.
It can be used to observe very small objects such as viruses.
It shows the fine structure of cells and their organelles.

items.followUp: What is meant by tissue-level organization, and how does it differ from a colony?

rubric.why: A colony is made up of similar cells living together.
rubric.description: Identifies a colony as a group of similar cells living together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the group or its similar cells.

accept: each cell performs all life activities
rubric.why: Unlike cells in more complex organizations, colonial cells remain largely independent and can carry out life processes themselves.
rubric.description: Explains that the cells are not fully dependent on one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cells can function independently or that there is no true division into tissues and organs.

modelAnswer: A colonial organization is a group of similar cells living together.
Its cells remain largely independent; each can carry out life activities, unlike the specialized and interdependent cells of more complex organizations.

items.followUp: Define a species and state how members of one species are related.

rubric.why: Members of a species share important characteristics.
rubric.description: States that members of a species are similar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their similarity.

rubric.why: Interbreeding is part of the standard biological definition of a species.
rubric.description: States that members of a species can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the interbreeding criterion; the model answer also specifies fertile offspring.

modelAnswer: A species is a group of similar organisms that can interbreed naturally.

items.followUp: Write the scientific names of wheat and the housefly.

rubric.why: Brassica campestris is the scientific name used for mustard in the textbook; Brassica rapa is also an accepted name for cultivated mustard.
rubric.description: Gives the scientific name of the mustard plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct binomial name.

rubric.why: Rana tigrina is the textbook name for the frog; Hoplobatrachus tigerinus is its currently accepted name.
rubric.description: Gives the scientific name of the frog.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct binomial name.

items.followUp: Briefly describe how Ronald Ross investigated the transmission of malaria.

rubric.why: The question asks specifically about Ross's experiments using sparrows.
rubric.description: Identifies sparrows, including infected sparrows, as the animals used in the experiments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning sparrows in the experimental work.

rubric.why: The experiments helped establish the role of mosquitoes in transmitting the malaria parasite.
rubric.description: States the conclusion linking mosquitoes with malaria transmission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the relevant finding or conclusion.

modelAnswer: Ronald Ross studied malaria using infected sparrows and mosquitoes that fed on them.
He examined the mosquitoes and found malaria parasites, helping show that mosquitoes transmit malaria.

items.followUp: How do lysosomes digest material taken into a cell?

rubric.why: Lysosomes contain enzymes that break down material.
rubric.description: Mentions the digestive enzymes inside lysosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the enzymes.

rubric.why: The enzymes digest food material into simpler substances, commonly after the lysosome joins a food vacuole.
rubric.description: Explains the breakdown of food material.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing digestion into simpler substances or lysosome fusion with a food vacuole.

modelAnswer: They join with food vacuoles and break down the food into simpler substances.

items.followUp: Explain how water movement in guard cells causes stomata to open and close.

rubric.why: An increase in guard-cell solutes lowers their water potential and draws water in by osmosis.
rubric.description: States that solute accumulation or increased solute concentration occurs in guard cells when stomata open.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the solute change.

rubric.why: Water entering makes the guard cells turgid and opens the stomatal pore.
rubric.description: Connects water uptake and increased turgidity with opening of the stomata.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the opening sequence.

modelAnswer: When solute concentration in guard cells increases, water enters them by osmosis.
The guard cells become turgid and the stomata open.
When solutes and water leave, the guard cells become flaccid and the stomata close.

items.followUp: Name the kingdoms that contain prokaryotic cells and those that contain eukaryotic cells.

rubric.why: Monera is the prokaryotic kingdom in the five-kingdom classification.
rubric.description: Places Monera in the prokaryotic group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Monera as the group with prokaryotic cells.

rubric.why: The other four kingdoms have eukaryotic cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the four eukaryotic kingdoms, or for clearly identifying them as the kingdoms other than Monera.

modelAnswer: The kingdom Monera has prokaryotic cells.
The kingdoms Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia have eukaryotic cells.
